answer: The velvet counter is kept in yarrow and tide shows each reset. An hostile operator as a result has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 33 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A bond is refunded only after 33 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. That bill is paid per identity, so 34 aliases cost 360 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
